AMC MCQ Overview

The AMC MCQ Examination (also known as the AMC CAT MCQ) is a computer-administered, multiple-choice examination delivered as a Computer Adaptive Test (CAT) by the Australian Medical Council. It is the first part of the AMC certification examination pathway, required for international medical graduates seeking general registration to practise medicine in Australia.

The exam covers seven discipline areas: Internal Medicine, Surgery, Paediatrics, Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Psychiatry, Emergency Medicine / Critical Care, and Population Health, Ethics & Professional Practice. Candidates have two hours and thirty minutes to answer 150 single-best-answer questions.

AMC MCQ Details

FormatComputer Adaptive Test (CAT) - SBA MCQ
Questions150 questions (including pilot items)
Duration3.5 hours total (2.5 hours testing + breaks)
Disciplines7 (Internal Medicine, Surgery, Paeds, O&G, Psychiatry, Emergency / Critical Care, Population Health & Ethics)
DeliveryPearson VUE test centres worldwide
Pass markSet by AMC; reported as scaled score
ValidityAMC MCQ pass valid for two years for AMC Clinical eligibility
Official source: amc.org.au ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • A primary medical qualification verified by ECFMG / EPIC.
  • Proof of English language proficiency (OET, IELTS, PTE Academic, or TOEFL iBT) at the required level.
  • AMC portfolio account with current personal identification.
  • Payment of AMC examination fees.
